newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast crudes edge higher, local trade thin - May 6.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast crudes edge higher, local trade thin - May 6.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crudes edged higher Tuesday, tracking West Texas Intermediate/Cushing (WTI), but local markets turned inactive as traders scheduled next month's crude shipments to refineries, traders said.
West Coast traders said demand for regional crudes thinned as Tosco Marketing Corp (TMC) brought in large volumes of South American crudes.
The company is testing how well the grades run at refineries acquired from Unocal Corp, traders said.
"Apparently, they're running oil through all of their refineries to test it out," said a crude oil marketer.
Tosco confirmed last week they bought a 360,000-barrel cargo of Cano Limon from Colombia's state oil company, Ecopetrol, for $2.97 a barrel under June WTI.
The crude will be loaded June 13-23 and takes two weeks to reach West Coast refiners.
Traders also waited to see which West Coast reiners would buy light crude available in June and July from the Elk Hills Naval Petroleum Reserve.
The region's ample supply of foreign crude dulled interest in last week's Elk Hills auction, which saw only 11,025 of 16,100 barrels-per-day purchased.
Oil pipelines and refineries were unscathed early Tuesday by an earthquake that rocked northeast Kern County, the state's largest oil producing area.
The quake measured 4.4 on the Richter scale.
"I've been here all day and I haven't felt a thing," said a spokeswoman at Texaco's Bakersfield 57,000 bpd refinery.
Kern River crude was unchanged at $13.86/13.96 a barrel, with discounts 20 to 10 cents below postings. Traders said Friday's drop in postings could force producers to narrow discounts.
Wilmington and Line 63 markets remained dormant.
